item.title: A brief history of the Ort case
item.description:
Mrs. Ort filed for divorce in New Jersey state court. According to the authors of this site, she did so without the permission of a Beis Din; R’ Avraham was not consulted by the rav she spoke to regarding the monetary issues. A letter signed by three Lakewood Roshei Yeshiva and Rav Dovid Feinstein did not reverse the filing.

June 2000. R’ Avraham moved back into the family home to attempt a reconciliation, remaining for fourteen months. During this time he consented to the release of over $300,000 from the couple’s joint account. All accounts had been frozen at filing, as is usual, to prevent dissipation of assets before settlement.

item.title: An Open Letter to Mrs. Manya Ort
item.description:
Dear Mrs. Ort, עמו׳ש

Sometimes, people are traveling a contain road, and they suddenly look around and realize they’ve been heading in the wrong direction. They’re not where they wanted to go, but rather they are getting further from their destination. It happens on the highway driving seventy miles an hour on the eastbound road when you need to go west. It also happens in life.

So, what do you do then? You’ve invested time, effort and fuel in getting to this point, but it’s neither wise nor productive to keep going in the same diction.

item.title: For Shame!
item.description:
Posted February 3, 2013.

Scans: the writs whose publication this exchange defends — ksav siruv, Baltimore Bais Din (2002) .

Terry K. writes:

Such a shame that such things are publicized in our community!

Our response:

In OUR community, we try to establish our norms b y the guidelines of Chazal as codified in the poskim. In the classic Halachic treatise Chofetz Chaim (4:8) we find: “If Bais Din tells someone a halacha… and he absolutely refuses t o acquiesce, and he has no valid reason for doing so, it is permitted to publicize his iniquity.” (See footnote 32 that this publicity is permitted only for a practical purpose eg. “to motivate the culprit to desist from his wrongdoing by utilizing the opprobrium of public opinion.”) This i s further elaborated on ibid, 10:4.

item.title: How Sad!
item.description:
A fellow Jew writes:

So terrible a yid has to be forced to flee! If all of these documents are true, what’s going on? It doesn’t make sense how could this be?!

Our response:

We appreciate your sympathy for the situation. Yes it is terrible, and Yes, it doesn’t make sense. What does Mrs. Ort gain from forcing R’ Avrohom into golus for almost two years now, and forcibly removing the children’s father from their lives?

item.title: One-Sided?

Yossi Writes:

While I don’t claim to know both sides of this story it is quite clear to me that this site is not just to provide information. This is rather a forum for a one sided story t o be told.

I do however know some well respected people that have worked for Mrs. Ort because they are aware of the details that represent her case.

item.title: R' Efryim Dovid Gruskin
item.description:
Who he is in this story

R’ Efryim Dovid Gruskin, Mrs. Manya Ort’s brother-in-law, described in the correspondence as a former Rosh Yeshiva. Two open letters address him — asking him to reflect on the counsel he has given his sister-in-law, and challenging his reported description of her as “penniless” and “starving.”

The first letter: a call to reflect

The letter grants that his advice was surely given with her best interests in mind, then asks him to look at where the road traveled under that advice has led — “Can you honestly say that it has led in the direction of peace, closure and resolution of the conflicts that have been tearing this family apart?”

item.title: Stop mailing me!
item.description:
‘Stop Involving Me’ writes:

Phshata Yid,

why was your letter sent to me?

I have no interest in knowing other people’s business. Is this case getting attention because there is 5 million dollars involved? Pushita Yid says: If you (or anyone else) wish to be deleted from our mailing list, we would be happy to comply. Simply let us know who you are so that we can do so.

item.title: The $139,258 check
item.description:
This check is presented as evidence against the claim that the Ort family was left with nothing.

What the document shows:

  • Drawer: Philip Ort Real Estate Account, Brooklyn NY
  • Check #1057, dated 2/16/10
  • Payee: Manya Ort
  • Amount: $139,258.00
  • Handwritten note on the face: “Accepted as payment IN FULL for all monies outstanding to all Ort Children without RESERVATION. If that’s not acceptable, DON’T DEPOSIT THIS CHECK. I’m NOT going to go through all these figures AGAIN, under ANY CIRCUMSTANCE.”

What it does and doesn’t prove. The check documents a $139,258 payment from the real-estate account to Mrs. Ort in February 2010. The handwritten note frames it as a conditional full settlement of outstanding child-related monies — conditional because it instructs the recipient not to deposit it if the “in full” characterization is not accepted. Whether it settled the claims is a question for the underlying dispute; the scan alone records the offer and the condition.

item.title: The Adler Story
item.description:
What happened, according to the documents

R’ Avraham Ort’s mother passed away in November 1999. In January 2000, Mrs. Manya Ort moved $350,000 out of her late mother-in-law’s account at Discount Bank and wired it to an Israel account of Mrs. Ort Sr. that already held $250,000. She then gave the combined $600,000 to her cousin R’ Ira (Yitzchak) Adler of Monsey, NY, with instructions to disburse it to “a yeshiva” — which yeshiva was never named.

item.title: The Brodericks
item.description:
Who they are in this story

Mrs. Soro Rochel (Sarah) Broderick, a married daughter of R’ Avrohom Ort, and her husband R’ Ranaan Broderick. Correspondence signed “the true friends of the Brodericks” lays out three financial issues and a parallel dispute over whether the family would submit to a Din Torah.

The three financial issues, as the correspondence presents them

  1. Custodial accounts. Over $180,000 in cash that Mrs. Broderick acquired by taking ownership of custodial accounts her father had established in her name. A Salomon Smith Barney letter of September 2002, confirming the account history going back to December 1999, is cataloged: catalog entry — view the letter .

  2. Real estate that R’ Avrohom inherited from his parents and placed in her name as a legal tax shelter, which she assumed control of.

  3. Substantial income generated by the above.

item.title: The Steinbergs
item.description:
Background

Rabbi Yisroel Steinberg and Mrs. Miriam Steinberg of Lakewood — Mrs. Steinberg is described in the correspondence as Mrs. Manya Ort’s friend since kindergarten. A series of open letters addressed to the couple argues that they publicly portrayed Mrs. Ort as “penniless” and “starving,” and urges them to call on her to bring the dispute to a Beis Din.

The $3,000 chesed loan

According to the letters, Rabbi Steinberg — then president of the g’mach of Cong. Zichron Shneur — arranged a $3,000 “chesed loan” for Mrs. Ort. The letters quote his July 2002 deposition: “she said she needed $3,000 and… I wrote out the check.”

item.title: What Would You Do With a Check Like That?
item.description:
COMMENT:

From: a friend of the Ort family

Message: with a check like that, if was a single parent to thirteen children, i would pay my mortgage, utility bills, tuition, food bills, etc… very stupid question!!!!

REPLY:

We found it very surprising that you seemngly forget the most basic information that has been on display on this website since its inception.

item.title: Who Went to Court, and Who to Beis Din?
item.description:
The question

As posed in the correspondence: the impression from Mrs. Ort’s camp is that only after R’ Avrohom took her to secular court and lost is he now insisting on Beis Din — and since he accepted binding arbitration, why is he complaining? This page answers with documents.

Who filed first

Page 8 of the Final Arbitration Ruling, headed “Procedural History,” states that Mrs. Ort filed the divorce complaint on February 4, 2000, accompanied by an Order to Show Cause freezing assets — including the children’s and the Dove Foundation’s assets — and that a March 6, 2000 order continued the restraint: catalog entry — view .

We respond:

item.title: Why Isn’t There Enough Money There?
item.description:
‘Really?!?’ writes:

The documentation presented implies that right now, today, the family is the recipient of $11,000 a month in monthly support drawn upon the accounts in the names of the unmarried children. Is this true? Doesn’t this satisfy court ordered child support? Why is R’ Avraham (did I read correctly?) out of the country and unable to see his children. Is there a court order stating he must stay away from his children? Are armed guards around his children that prevent his seeing the children?

item.title: Why this site exists
item.description: This site was created to provide information. It has been said that because R’ Avraham Ort left his family penniless, Mrs. Ort was forced to turn to the secular courts. This site presents the other side of the story — documentation that, according to its authors, shows Mrs. Ort received millions of dollars in liquid assets over the years, in addition to real estate, while R’ Avraham was left with the child-support obligations.

item.title: Wicked As Can Be?
item.description:
A Friend writes:

I am going through a divorce myself with similarly very wicked people. My wife has made claims of child abuse which were found to be unfounded and has gone to arko’oys instead of bais din.

At least in Lakewood, people take halocho seriously. In Brooklyn one has these so-called botei din who side with the woman even if she goes to arko’oys. Hashem yerachem on this innocent man. The community needs to shun and ostracize these people and their supporters. Only this will help.
